findings.title: Passkey condition is inverted: passkeys are now only offered once a user is already set.
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns true only when `user != null`. The old code filled the WebAuthn form only when no user was selected (`context.getUser() == null`). Both `authenticate` (line 115) and `challenge` (line 137) now skip `fillContextForm` on a normal first login, where no user is set yet. On that path the conditional-UI passkey form and the `webauth` element no longer render, and a failed password attempt also drops them because it clears the user. That breaks the tests in this PR that expect the form on a fresh login page. In the other direction, any re-authenticating user gets passkey UI even if they have no passkey credential. The condition should be `currentUser == null || currentUser.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`.

findings.title: Calls a no-argument `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` that is not defined in the code shown.
findings.body: The only definition added is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in `UsernamePasswordForm`. Unless a no-argument overload exists in code I can't see, this line will not compile. Even if one exists, it ignores the current user, so the username form is never skipped during re-authentication once passkeys are on, even for users who have no passkey. Pass `context.getUser()` so it uses the same per-user check as `UsernamePasswordForm`.
